verdict.line: Buy. A 3-bed here at about $3,350 psf is at or below what the closest competitors' 3-bed-size resales support (about $3,450 psf as a new launch). 2-bed is the most wanted size in this rental and investment area. The 4-bed has a very thin resale pool: buy only to live in.
reasons: The closest competitors (Sky Everton, Spottiswoode Suites, Spottiswoode 18, Spottiswoode Residences) work out to about $3,450 psf as a brand-new launch, after adding 5% where they were not built under the harmonised floor-area rules, a 24% new-launch premium (what launches selling now in the CCR charge over their closest resale, 7 launches).

compsNote: 4 of the 4 competitors are within 1 km. Near-twins come first: up to two condos within 1.5 km with a similar number of homes (half to double) completed in 2016 or later. Then every suitable condo within 1 km (same tenure, completed 2011 or later first), widening to 2 km and 3 km only if fewer than 3; executive condos are left out. Resale prices are URA medians for the last 6 months where there were at least 5 resales, otherwise the last 12 months. Condos launched before June 2023 measured their areas under the old rules (including air-con ledges), so their psf is raised 5% to compare like for like.
priceDecide: Like for like by size: for each unit type we take each resale competitor's average psf for units within about 15% of that size (last 6 months, or 12 or 24 if too few). Each is raised by the 24% new-launch premium that launches selling now in the CCR carry over their closest resale (7 launches). Buy at or below = the average of the competitors' new-launch equivalents for that size; walk away above = 5% more. 2-bed: buy at or below $3,220, walk away above $3,380, this project about $3,168 psf; 3-bed: buy at or below $3,450, walk away above $3,620, this project about $3,351 psf; 4-bed: buy at or below $3,220, walk away above $3,380, this project about $4,230 psf. This project's price by unit type is from the developer's caveats.  No developer floor can be worked out: the developers already owned the land.

gain.costs: Potential gain is after Buyer's Stamp Duty at IRAS rates, about $6,000 legal fees and a 2% agent fee plus 9% GST when you sell. Loan interest, property tax, maintenance and rent are not included.

exit.note: How we test each buyer group, in today's money (prices, HDB values and incomes tend to rise together): the unit at today's current average price; a 25% down payment plus Buyer's Stamp Duty; HDB upgraders put their flat's sale proceeds in first (median resale price, minus an illustrative $150,000 loan). The group can buy if that capital covers the down payment and stamp duty; the income the remaining 30-year loan needs (tested at 4% under the 55% TDSR) is shown against SingStat's 2025 averages by home type, excluding employer CPF (4-room $11,097, 5-room and executive $13,887, condo $22,006). HDB resale prices rose 4.2% a year over the past 10 years, so upgraders' capital usually grows too. Singaporean HDB owners who buy before selling pay 20% Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty upfront and get it back only if they sell the flat within 6 months (IRAS).

fplans.note: Main layout per bedroom type (most units where counts are published), redrawn from the developers' plans in the Stacked Homes directory. Score out of 10, same rules for every plan: start at 4; +1 regular shape, dumbbell, kitchen that can be closed off, kitchen or yard window, AC ledge and planter under 5%, store or shelter or utility room; −1 long corridor, ledge and planter 10% or more, balcony over 12%. Efficiency = the share of the area not taken by AC ledges, planters, bay windows and corridors. Plans under the 2023 rules exclude AC ledges from the strata area, so their sq ft is all usable.
